assumptions.assumption: Moving objects can be reliably detected by lidar points that are not inside any static obstacle
assumptions.why: first_not_on_map entries show non‑map points detected at ~1.5 m before robot stalls

assumptions.assumption: A lateral bypass waypoint 2 m to the side of the object is always reachable
assumptions.why: controller often fails to find a bypass target and enters indefinite stop‑wait

assumptions.assumption: Velocity‑Obstacle sampling will always yield at least one safe (v,w) candidate
assumptions.why: best_score == -inf occurs, causing the robot to wait forever

assumptions.assumption: Critical‑stop detection (dist ≤ 0.8 m) prevents collisions before they happen
assumptions.why: no critical stop triggered yet robot stalls far before the 0.8 m threshold

assumptions.assumption: A brief stop‑wait (0.5 s) after failed bypass is enough to let the moving object pass
assumptions.why: the robot repeatedly re‑enters stop‑wait without ever resuming motion

approach_families.family: simple detection + stop + rotate (no bypass, no VO)
approach_families.result: ≈13/43 passes (best single family, turn 2 gave 7/10 passes)

candidates.idea: Replace the complex bypass/VO logic with a minimal state machine: use only front‑cone detection (≤1.2 m, ±30°). When a moving point is seen, stop and rotate away for a fixed 1 s, then resume waypoint tracking.
candidates.for: high pass rate of the simple stop‑rotate approach (turn 2) and to avoid stall caused by missing bypass targets
candidates.risk: may increase travel time; occasional false positives could cause unnecessary rotations

candidates.idea: Compute a continuous repulsion vector from all moving points (inverse‑square weighting) and blend it with the waypoint direction; scale forward speed by the distance to the nearest moving point, never fully stopping unless an object is <0.5 m.
candidates.for: provides smooth avoidance without dead‑end stop‑wait loops
candidates.risk: repulsion may push robot into static obstacles if not carefully clamped

candidates.idea: Run a lightweight DWA with a longer horizon (2 s) and, if no safe candidate exists, fall back to a low‑speed mode (0.2‑0.5 m/s) instead of waiting, while still using the existing VO functions.
candidates.for: prevents the controller from stalling when the VO set is empty
candidates.risk: low‑speed mode may still be too slow to clear a moving object before it returns

diagnosis.chosen: Candidate 1 – adopt the simple front‑cone stop‑rotate state machine, because it matches the historically most successful family and eliminates the bypass/VO dead‑ends.
diagnosis.target: controller logic (state machine, detection, waypoint tracking) – remove bypass/VO code and add a minimal stop‑rotate state.
diagnosis.direction: 1. Add constants _DETECT_DIST_CLOSE=1.2, _DETECT_ANGLE_CLOSE=np.deg2rad(30), _ROT_TIME=1.0, _AVOID_ROT_SPEED=1.2. 2. Initialize persistent variables controller.state='normal' and controller.rotate_end=0.0. 3. At each step call a new _detect_moving_front(pose) that uses only the front lidar, distance ≤_DETECT_DIST_CLOSE and bearing within ±_DETECT_ANGLE_CLOSE, filtering static obstacles. 4. If state=='normal' and a moving object is detected, set controller.state='rotate', controller.rotate_end=t+_ROT_TIME, and command v=0, w=_AVOID_ROT_SPEED*sign(bearing). 5. While state=='rotate' keep v=0, w as above until t>=controller.rotate_end, then set state back to 'normal'. 6. In 'normal' state follow the existing waypoint list using simple proportional heading control (v=_MAX_SPEED*max(0,cos(yaw_err)), w=_KP_W*yaw_err) and skip all bypass/VO functions.
